title: feat: flat design for the enter dashboard
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Flattens the Enter dashboard and the shared `@pollinations/ui` surfaces. Depth comes from tint steps instead of shadows; only floating layers (menus, tooltips) keep one.

- Removes resting shadows: desk → block → card are one tint step apart, with `rounded-block` / `rounded-card` radius tokens. Light mode stays close to main (cream blocks, white cards); dark mode goes near-black
- Keeps main's component colours and button rule (filled buttons navigate, outlined buttons write); large buttons carry 16px text, which also applies to Playground and Websim
- One 12px shell gap sets the page rhythm, the sidebar drops its outer rule, and on phones blocks run edge to edge
- Top-up: the slider picks the pack and the fee-inclusive total shows once, on the Buy button, with the fee and tax note under it (no hover tooltip); Buy and Save share one row so both sliders match
- Info badges centre on their line; Delete account aligns left on phones

Every `@pollinations/ui` consumer (playground, websim, react showcase, economics, kpi, model-monitor, observability, flow) picks up the flat surfaces. The pollinations.ai website doesn't import these styles.

Preview on staging data: https://flat1.enter.pollinations.ai

gist.headline: Less shadow, more garden
gist.blurb: Enter got a flatter coat of paint: tinted surfaces do the work shadows used to do. The top-up button now shows the fee-inclusive total right where you buy.
gist.summary: The Enter dashboard and shared @pollinations/ui surfaces now use tint steps instead of resting shadows, with a 12px shell gap, edge-to-edge mobile blocks, and a top-up Buy button that shows the fee-inclusive total.
gist.impact: Enter and other @pollinations/ui apps, including Playground and Websim, get the flatter layout; top-up users can see the full total on Buy, with the fee and tax note directly below.
gist.visual_concept: Show the Enter dashboard as a cozy pixel-art workbench: cream desk, lightly tinted blocks, and white cards stacked by color rather than shadows. Polli adjusts a top-up slider beside a prominent Buy button showing a total; a small code-plant and the CRT monitor robot make the shared interface feel like part of a growing garden.

The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she wears tiny designer glasses, stays small-to-medium within the scene, and is strictly pixel art, never realistic — cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, with dark purple (#110518) outlines and no resting shadows.
